output.summary: An annual herb native to the United Kingdom and widespread across several temperate regions, water pepper grows in damp ground and shallow water. It has narrow leaves, nodding flower spikes and a pungent taste; wild plants can irritate skin. Cultivated East Asian varieties are eaten, including leaves, young sprouts and seeds.
output.edibilityNote: In East Asia, cultivated varieties are eaten; Japanese cooks use leaves as a vegetable, young sprouts as garnish, and seeds with wasabi.
